column1: # resources | objective | solo activity | self-check question | correct | foil
i,ɪ|Read sounds through spelling|Write the sound shared by seat and scene. Say both before looking at the letters.|Which stays alike at the start of both words?|The /s/ sound|The whole spelling
eɪ,æ|Separate gliding and steady vowels|Say late and lap slowly. Keep one vowel steady and let the other move.|Which word needs a glide?|late|lap
b,p|Compare voiced and voiceless lip closures|Say bin and pin with a hand in front of your mouth. Replay the beginnings.|Which word starts with /p/?|pin|bin
s,z|Hear final friction|Alternate ice and eyes at the end of an invitation. Listen to the buzz and the preceding vowel.|Which ends in /z/?|eyes|ice
d,t|Choose a tongue-tip stop|Give the names Dawn and Tom over the phone. Compare how their first sounds release.|Which starts with a typically voiceless stop?|Tom|Dawn
i,ɛ|Hear close and mid front vowels|Say neat and net. Let your jaw open slightly on the second word.|Which has the more open vowel?|net|neat
ə,ɪ|Hear vowels in light syllables|Record lemon and limit. Compare the light syllables in the modeled readings.|Which symbol represents the relaxed vowel in lemon?|ə|aɪ
f,v|Distinguish lip friction with voice|Say leaf and leave in separate requests. Check how long air can continue.|Which word ends with voiced friction?|leave|leaf
ɡ,k|Separate back stops|Alternate coat and goat in a guessing game. Keep the place of closure stable.|What mainly stays alike?|Place of closure|Whether voicing is present
h,w,j|Compare three ways to begin a vowel|Mime heat, wheat and yeast. Feel breath, lip rounding and front-tongue movement.|Which begins with rounded lips?|wheat|heat
aɪ,ɪ|Read vowel spellings in context|Ask for a bite, then a bit. Keep the second vowel steady.|Which has a moving vowel?|bite|bit
ʃ,dʒ,tʃ|Distinguish frication from a closure and release|Record shop, chop and job. Identify the beginning that can be held as friction alone.|Which starts with continuous friction?|shop|chop
l,ɹ|Separate two liquid consonants|Tell a friend whether to take the lane or wait for rain. Notice tongue-tip contact.|Which begins with /l/?|lane|rain

ɑ,ɛɹ|Read British and American vowel-plus-r patterns|Compare the models for car and care. Trace how the American r affects the ending.|Which British citation spelling fits care in this course?|/keə/|/kɑː/
m,n,ŋ|Change the closure for nasal endings|Hum through sum, sun and sung. Move the closure while keeping the air nasal.|Where is the closure for sung?|Back of tongue|Lips
oʊ,ɒ|Contrast a glide with a short British vowel|Listen to the UK model of pot and the US model of coat. Say each in a shopping request.|Which UK symbol is used for the vowel in pot?|ɒ|əʊ
θ,ð|Make dental friction with and without voice|Alternate thin and then. Touch your throat lightly as the air passes.|Which begins with voiced friction?|then|thin
ʌ,ʊ,u|Identify three vowel regions|Record luck, look and Luke. Compare rounding and tongue height.|Which uses /ʊ/?|look|Luke
ɝ,ɔ|Read stressed r-colored vowels|Say bird and board. Then compare their British reference readings.|Which contains American /ɝ/?|bird|board
ɔɪ,aʊ|Distinguish two vowel paths|Say toy and town. Trace the direction your lips move near the end.|Which glide ends with increased rounding?|town|toy
syllables|Count spoken syllables|Tap once for each vowel beat in banana and window. Check your count on replay.|How many syllables are in banana?|Three|Two
longstress|Locate the main syllable|Say technique and develop while tapping each syllable. Make only one tap strongest.|Where is the main stress in technique?|Second syllable|First syllable
emphasis|Find the main beat of a sentence|Answer “Who sent it?” and “What did you send?” using the same line. Shift the beat.|In reply to Who, which word can carry the strongest beat?|I|note
startcluster|Build syllable beginnings|Build the start of spring one consonant at a time, then join the word.|How many consonants come before the vowel in spring?|Three|Two
clusters|Keep syllable endings together|Say help slowly and then normally. Listen for the two consonants after the vowel.|Which ending belongs to help?|/lp/|/ləp/
plural|Choose a plural ending from sound|Compare bags, books and buses. Count the final syllables.|Which adds a syllable?|buses|books
past|Hear the three regular past endings|Read packed, called and waited in a short account. Listen for extra syllables.|Which adds a syllable to its base?|waited|packed
stress|Use stress to identify a word's job|Say record in “a record” and “record this”. Match the reading to the intended job.|Which has initial stress in this pair?|The noun|The verb

compound|Distinguish a compound from a description|Tell a gardener about a greenhouse, then describe a house painted green.|Which names a plant building?|The compound greenhouse|The description green house
longstress|Find the beat in a long word|Break develop into syllables, rebuild it, and say it in your own sentence.|Which syllable stands out in develop?|vel|op
family|Track stress through a word family|Say photograph, photography and photographic. Mark the strongest syllable in each.|Where is the main beat in photography?|Second syllable|First syllable

rhythm|Hear a row of strong beats|Tap the key words in “Stop. Look. Listen.” Then say them as quick instructions.|Which version makes three separate warnings?|Three distinct beats|One long unstressed run
weak|Reduce words around a main beat|Offer to drive with a light can. Repeat as a correction with a stronger can.|Which reading answers a doubt about ability?|Strong CAN|Light can
negative|Protect meaning in contractions|Replay a positive and negative reply. Listen for the part that reverses the meaning.|Which denies sending something?|I didn't send it|I did send it
pronouns|Move focus to or away from a pronoun|Give a direction about a recipient. Repeat it to correct the item instead.|When correcting the recipient, emphasize which word?|her|ticket
aux|Hear short auxiliary verbs|Offer a possibility, then firmer advice. Listen to could and should.|Which expresses advice in this pair?|should|could
weak|Keep small function words light|Say “Send a note to Lee.” Mark the destination and reduce to in a neutral reading.|Which word names the destination?|Lee|to
link|Join a consonant to the next vowel|Say pick it up in one flow, then compare with three isolated words.|Where is a consonant followed by a vowel?|pick it|the start of pick

reduction|Listen for changes at word boundaries|Compare a careful next week with a quicker version. Keep the timing recoverable.|Which detail should be preserved?|The intended week|A pause after every word
link|Compare vowel-to-vowel transitions|Say go out and see it. Notice a rounded or front glide between vowels.|Which may contain a w-like transition?|go out|see it
checking|Check a detail you missed|Hear a plan, ask about the uncertain date, then repeat the confirmed information.|Which reply requests clarification?|Thursday, did you say?|Thursday is fine.

quote|Turn written punctuation into speech|Read a question quoted inside a statement. Use a short boundary to mark the quotation.|What marks the start of the quoted voice?|A change in grouping or pitch|Reading the quotation marks as words

group|Put boundaries between ideas|Say the time first, then give the invitation. Move the boundary and listen again.|Which grouping keeps the time together?|After work / let's eat|After / work let's eat
continue|Signal that your turn continues|List two items and leave space for a third, then repeat as a completed list.|What does the unfinished reading invite?|Another item|An immediate goodbye
story|Sequence a short story|Tell two events, signaling the change with then. Listen for distinct groups.|Which word helps order the second event?|then|very
smalltalk|Open a social exchange|Comment on the weather and leave an opening for a response.|Which reply continues small talk?|Has it been warm all week?|Turn left now.
instructions|Confirm a direction|Hear a short route, repeat its landmark, and correct the wrong turn.|Which detail changes between left and right?|Direction|Meeting time
quote|Separate a quoted voice|Introduce a friend's words and rehearse the quote with a different pitch range.|Which phrase announces another speaker?|She asked|In my bag
emphasis|Choose emphatic stress|Disagree with who sent a message while keeping the rest of the reply light.|Which word corrects the sender in “I sent it”?|I|it
addition|Highlight a newly added detail|Add a coat to an existing list. Put the main beat on the item being added.|Which is new information?|coat|the existing list
given|Place emphasis on important information|Answer when and who questions with the same statement. Move just the main beat.|Which detail answers when?|Monday|Nina
contrast|Contrast alternatives with prominence|Correct the color, then correct the object. Listen for which word carries the contrast.|Which word contrasts blue with green?|blue|folder
booking|Repair a misunderstood booking|Correct the number while keeping seats light. Repeat to correct the object instead.|Which word needs prominence when correcting fifty to fifteen?|fifteen|seats
topic|Introduce a new topic|Use a short opening group before asking about Friday. Listen for the topic boundary.|Which introduces a topic?|As for Friday…|See you later.

checking|Distinguish checking from accepting|Ask for confirmation and then acknowledge the same news with the same word.|What does the modeled rising reading do here?|Requests confirmation|Closes the discussion
asking|Choose a tone for a real question|Ask where someone lives, then check a guess about their address.|Which turn checks an existing guess?|You live here?|Where do you live?
given|Separate given and new information|A friend already knows the person. Say when you met and bring forward the day.|Which information is new?|The day|The person

asking|End a statement with a checking tag|Say “We're early, aren't we?” first as a genuine question, then seeking agreement.|Which reading invites a real answer?|The uncertain check|The confident agreement

attitude|Agree or disagree with a tone|Try a tentative and a confident reading of sure. Match each to the situation.|Which situation invites a tentative check?|You doubt the arrangement|You are confirming a settled plan

attitude|Use a higher pitch range for involvement|Say the same news with an ordinary range and with a higher starting pitch. Compare the attitude you intended.|Which change directly raises pitch range?|Start the voice higher|Increase playback volume

i,ɪ,ə|Look up IPA symbols|Read each target symbol before playing its word. Use the chart to build an unseen example.|Which resource tells you sounds directly?|A phonemic transcription|The number of letters

i,ɪ,θ,plural,booking|Sample your starting skills|Try each check without its model first. Record listening, transcription and message interpretation separately.|What should you review after confusing two sounds by ear?|Another listening contrast|Only the spelling

θ,clusters,plural|Choose a personal focus|Use a sound from your own speech or teacher notes. Test it on a fresh word before choosing a goal.|Which is evidence about your needs?|Your own repeated listening difficulty|Your first language alone

i,ɪ,ɛ,æ,p,b,s,z|Look up contrasting sounds|Pick a pair, predict the difference, then compare its two words and a new example.|What changes in a minimal pair?|One sound and the word's meaning|Every sound

given,contrast,booking|Build a phrasebook of main beats|Save a useful phrase and make two versions with different main beats.|What should each saved version include?|A situation that explains the focus|Only a word count

syllables,stress,group|Use pronunciation vocabulary|Illustrate syllable, stress and thought group with one spoken example of each.|Which is a group of words forming one idea?|A thought group|A consonant
